category: Metal Processing, Liquid & Gas Properties, Material Library and Heat/Moisture Supplements
description: COMSOL 6.4 Metal Processing Module (metallurgical phase transformations, austenite decomposition, alpha-beta titanium, carburization, quenching and induction hardening couplings), Liquid & Gas Properties Module topics complementary to the Thermodynamics entries of the reaction-engineering chunk (Java API, IAPWS water, reference state, XML export/import, transport models), the Material Library with material node types and property groups, and a few supplementary heat/moisture topics. Java strings are from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library model files.

tools.name: Metal Phase Transformation (metp)
tools.description: Metal Processing interface for diffusive, displacive and user-defined solid-state phase transformations in metals such as steels. It starts with two Metallurgical Phase nodes and one Phase Transformation node; any number of phases and transformations can be added, each transformation using Leblond-Devaux, JMAK, Kirkaldy-Venugopalan (simplified), Microstructure based, Koistinen-Marburger, Hyperbolic rate or user-defined kinetics. It can compute phase-composition-dependent effective thermal, electromagnetic and mechanical properties (a compound material), latent heat and transformation strains for Heat Transfer in Solids and Solid Mechanics.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Metal Phase Transformation. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("metp", "MetalPhaseTransformation", "geom1"); 0D version: physics().create("metp", "GlobalMetalPhaseTransformation")

parameters.name: Material Properties > Compute effective material properties
parameters.description: Create a compound material from the phase properties (matprops).

parameters.name: Heat Transfer > latentheat
parameters.description: Compute phase transformation latent heat (prop("HeatTransfer")).

parameters.name: Solid Mechanics > trip / plasticity / dilstrain / dilstraintype
parameters.description: Transformation-induced plasticity, per-phase plasticity, thermal/dilatation strains (strain based or density based).

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.description: Model input, e.g. from Heat Transfer in Solids or a prescribed history.

tools.notes: Only Time Dependent studies (Frequency-Transient with Magnetic Fields). Variables: metp.phase1.xi (phase fraction), metp.T, metp.Tt (temperature rate).

tools.name: Austenite Decomposition (audc)
tools.description: Specialized Metal Phase Transformation interface for hardening of steel from the austenitic state: it creates five phases (austenite, ferrite, pearlite, bainite, martensite) and four transformations (austenite to ferrite, pearlite, bainite and martensite) that are then configured with kinetic models and phase material data. The resulting compound material and latent heat/strain contributions are used by Heat Transfer in Solids and Solid Mechanics in quenching and induction hardening simulations.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Austenite Decomposition. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("audc", "AusteniteDecomposition", "geom1"); 0D: physics().create("audc", "GlobalAusteniteDecomposition")

parameters.name: Phases (phase1..phase5)
parameters.description: Austenite, Ferrite, Pearlite, Bainite, Martensite with Phase Material and initial fraction xi0.

parameters.name: Transformations (ptran1..ptran4)
parameters.description: Kinetic model per transformation (e.g. Leblond-Devaux for diffusive, Koistinen-Marburger for martensite).

parameters.name: Interface properties
parameters.description: latentheat, trip, plasticity, dilstrain (dilstraintype densitybased/strainbased).

tools.notes: The 0D GlobalAusteniteDecomposition is used to compute CCT/TTT diagrams and dilatometry curves (Transformation_Diagrams/transformation_diagram_computation, dilatometry_curves_from_cct).

tools.name: Austenite Decomposition, Kirkaldy-Venugopalan and Li-Niebuhr-Meekisho-Atteridge (interfaces)
tools.description: Two variants of the Austenite Decomposition interface that additionally create a Steel Composition node configured for composition-based kinetics: the Kirkaldy-Venugopalan framework expresses austenite decomposition in terms of ASTM grain size and alloy content (with optional Akerstrom-Oldenburg boron modification), and the Li-Niebuhr-Meekisho-Atteridge (LNMA) framework modifies it. The Phase Transformation nodes use the Microstructure based model with functions and transformation temperatures from the Steel Composition node, so only the chemistry and grain size are needed.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Austenite Decomposition, Kirkaldy-Venugopalan | Austenite Decomposition, Li-Niebuhr-Meekisho-Atteridge (default name audc)

parameters.name: Steel Composition > weight percent table
parameters.description: C, Mn, Si, Ni, Cr, Mo, ... in wt%.

parameters.name: G_ASTM
parameters.description: ASTM grain size number.

parameters.name: Phase transformation model formulation
parameters.description: Kirkaldy-Venugopalan or Li-Niebuhr-Meekisho-Atteridge; boron modification option.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Metal Processing > Austenite Decomposition, Li-Niebuhr-Meekisho-Atteridge
Steel Composition 1: C 0.4, Mn 0.7, Cr 1.0, Mo 0.2 wt%; G_ASTM = 8
Study: Time Dependent with a prescribed cooling rate to obtain final phase fractions and hardness
tools.notes: Type strings for these two variants are not used in the 6.4 Application Library Java files; model files show them as AusteniteDecomposition-based setups.

tools.name: Alpha-Beta Phase Transformation (abp)
tools.description: Specialized phase transformation interface for alpha-beta titanium alloys such as Ti-6Al-4V in welding and additive manufacturing: it creates three metallurgical phases and seven phase transformations with transformation conditions restricting some transformations to heating or cooling. Like the other phase transformation interfaces it can generate a phase-dependent compound material and latent heat/strain contributions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Alpha-Beta Phase Transformation. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("abp", "AlphaBetaPhaseTransformation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Phases
parameters.description: Beta and alpha phase variants (abp.phase1..phase3).

parameters.name: Phase transformations
parameters.description: Seven predefined transformations with heating/cooling conditions.

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.description: From a heat transfer interface with a moving welding/laser heat source.

tools.notes: Results: abp.phase1.xi etc. for final microstructure after the thermal cycle.

tools.name: Carburization (carb interface)
tools.description: Metal Processing interface that computes the evolving carbon mass fraction in a steel component exposed to a carbon-rich atmosphere by solving temperature-dependent carbon diffusion. The carbon potential of the environment is user defined (function of time) or a Boost-diffuse cycle (boost potential, diffuse potential, boost period); default nodes are Carburization, Initial Values and Zero Carbon Flux. The resulting carbon content feeds carbon-dependent phase transformation kinetics in quenching models.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Carburization. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("carb", "Carburization", "geom1"); model.component("comp1").physics("carb").prop("Carburization").set("carbmodel", "user")

parameters.name: carbmodel
parameters.description: user (carbon potential cpot) or boost-diffuse cycle (cboost, cdiffuse, tboost).

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.description: Temperature field used by the Arrhenius diffusion and mass transfer coefficients.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Quadratic by default; see 'Carburization Modeling' for mesh advice near surfaces.

tools.notes: Carbon variable carb.c. Nitriding is not a separate interface in COMSOL 6.4 (not found in the local documentation).

tools.name: Metallurgical Phase (Metal Processing)
tools.description: Node defining one metallurgical phase in a phase transformation interface: initial phase fraction, volume reference temperature, Phase Material, and per-phase heat transfer (k, rho, Cp), electromagnetic (sigma, mu_r, epsilon_r) and mechanical properties (E, nu, thermal expansion, initial yield stress, isotropic hardening model, weight factor for yield stress, soft phase). In 0D it also reports transformation times. These properties are mixed into the effective compound material.
tools.usage: Metal Phase Transformation / Austenite Decomposition > Metallurgical Phase (phaseN). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("metp").create("phase3", "MetallurgicalPhase", 2)

parameters.name: xi0
parameters.description: Initial phase fraction (e.g. 1 for austenite).

parameters.name: phaseMaterial
parameters.description: Material holding the phase properties (e.g. imported JMatPro phase materials).

parameters.name: k, rho, Cp, sigma, mur, E, nu, alpha
parameters.description: Phase properties (from_mat or user).

parameters.name: IsotropicHardeningModel, sigmags, Et
parameters.description: Per-phase plasticity (with Nonlinear Structural Materials or Geomechanics Module).

tools.notes: Phase fraction variable <tag>.phaseN.xi; the sum of fractions is checked (fraccheck, minpsum/maxpsum).

tools.name: Phase Transformation (Metal Processing: Leblond-Devaux, JMAK, Koistinen-Marburger)
tools.description: Node defining how a destination phase forms from a source phase. Models: Leblond-Devaux (formulations General coefficients K/L, Time and equilibrium, TTT diagram data, Parameterized TTT diagram) and Johnson-Mehl-Avrami-Kolmogorov (time/equilibrium/exponent, TTT data, parameterized TTT, fixed exponent) for diffusion-controlled transformations such as austenite to ferrite/pearlite/bainite; Koistinen-Marburger for displacive martensite formation driven by undercooling below Ms (beta coefficient or M90 temperature, optional stress modification); plus Kirkaldy-Venugopalan simplified, Microstructure based, Hyperbolic rate and User defined.
tools.usage: Phase transformation interface > Phase Transformation (ptranN). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("audc").create("ptran9", "PhaseTransformation", 2)

parameters.name: phasei / phasej
parameters.description: Source and destination phase.

parameters.name: ptModel
parameters.description: LeblondDevaux, JMAK, KoistinenMarburger, UserDefined, ... (Linear also seen in library models).

parameters.name: ldformulation / jmakformulation
parameters.description: KL (general coefficients) or ttt; xeqtaun (time, equilibrium, exponent) or ttt.

parameters.name: K, L / tau, n / beta, M90
parameters.description: Model coefficients, e.g. K(metp.T), L(metp.T) interpolation functions; Koistinen-Marburger beta = 0.011[1/K].

tools.notes: Each transformation also carries latent heat and TRIP parameters used by the couplings. Theory: 'Phase Transformation Models' in the Metal Processing Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Transformation Condition and Additional Source Phase (Metal Processing)
tools.description: Phase Transformation subnodes. Transformation Condition adds a Boolean expression that must hold for the transformation to proceed (e.g. metp.Tt<0[K/s] to allow it only during cooling); several conditions combine with AND, and smoothed conditions such as flc1hs(2*(a-b)/h, 1) improve convergence. Additional Source Phase lets further phases (e.g. a second austenite variant) contribute to forming the destination phase.
tools.usage: Phase Transformation > Transformation Condition (tc1) | Additional Source Phase (aphase1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("audc").feature("ptran9").create("aphase1", "AdditionalSourcePhase", -1)

parameters.name: Condition c
parameters.description: Boolean or smoothed expression, e.g. audc.Tt<0[K/s].

parameters.name: Additional source phase
parameters.description: Metallurgical phase contributing to the destination phase.

tools.notes: Transformation conditions are typical when a model contains both heating (austenitization) and cooling transformations.

tools.name: Steel Composition and Hardness (Metal Processing)
tools.description: Steel Composition specifies alloy weight percentages and derives transformation temperatures from empirical relations: Ae1/Ae3 (Andrews or parameterized), bainite start (Steven-Haynes or Kirkaldy-Venugopalan Bs) and martensite start (Andrews or Steven-Haynes Ms), optional equilibrium phase fractions (ferrite solubility, Hultgren extrapolation) and phase transformation functions for the Microstructure based model. Its Hardness subnode computes Vickers (Maynier et al., from phase fractions, composition and cooling rate at 700 degC) and Rockwell C hardness of the quenched steel.
tools.usage: Phase transformation interface > Steel Composition ; Steel Composition > Hardness

parameters.name: Weight percent of alloying elements
parameters.description: Table of wt% (C, Si, Mn, Ni, Cr, Mo, V, ...).

parameters.name: Ae1/Ae3, Bs, Ms models
parameters.description: Andrews / parameterized; Steven-Haynes / Kirkaldy-Venugopalan; Andrews / Steven-Haynes.

parameters.name: Hardness phase mapping
parameters.description: Select which phases represent ferrite, pearlite, bainite and martensite.

tools.example:
audc > Steel Composition 1: C 0.2, Mn 0.8, Cr 1.1, Ni 0.4 wt%; Ms model = Andrews
Steel Composition 1 > Hardness 1: ferrite=phase2, pearlite=phase3, bainite=phase4, martensite=phase5
Results: HV and HRC surface plots after quenching
tools.notes: Hardness is a post-cooling estimate valid for steels cooled from the austenitic state.

tools.name: Carburization, Carbon Flux, Zero Carbon Flux and Carbon Concentration (Carburization features)
tools.description: Nodes of the Carburization interface. Carburization (domain) sets the carbon diffusion coefficient - Arrhenius D = D0*exp(-QD/(R*T)) or user defined. Carbon Flux models mass transfer from the atmosphere with an Arrhenius or user mass transfer coefficient and the interface carbon potential or a user external concentration; Carbon Concentration prescribes the surface carbon content; Zero Carbon Flux (default) masks regions for selective carburization.
tools.usage: carb > Carburization (carb1), Carbon Flux (cflux1), Zero Carbon Flux (zflx1), Carbon Concentration. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("carb").create("cflux1", "CarbonFlux", 1)

parameters.name: diffusioncoefficient, D_0, Q_D, D
parameters.description: Arrhenius or user diffusion coefficient.

parameters.name: externalcarbonconcentration / c0
parameters.description: Carbon potential from the interface (potfrominterface) or user defined.

parameters.name: masstransfercoefficient, b_0, Q_b, b
parameters.description: Arrhenius or user mass transfer coefficient.

tools.notes: Theory: 'Carbon Potential Model' and carburization boundary conditions in the Metal Processing Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Heat Transfer with Phase Transformations (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface of the Metal Processing Module combining Heat Transfer in Solids with a Metal Phase Transformation interface and the Phase Transformation Latent Heat coupling. Use it for thermal processes where the microstructure evolution and its latent heat matter but stresses are not needed (e.g. annealing, heat treatment cycles, weld heat-affected zones).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Heat Transfer with Phase Transformations

parameters.name: Constituents
parameters.description: ht (Heat Transfer in Solids), metp (Metal Phase Transformation), lht1 coupling.

parameters.name: Compound material
parameters.description: Effective k, rho, Cp from phase fractions used by ht.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Metal Processing > Heat Transfer with Phase Transformations
Heat Flux (convective, quench oil htc(T)) on the surface
Study: Time Dependent 0-600 s
// Application Library: Metal_Processing_Module/Tutorial_Examples/phase_transformations_in_a_round_bar
tools.notes: Do not add latent heat as a separate Heat Source - the coupling already adds it.

tools.name: Steel Quenching (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface combining Heat Transfer in Solids, Austenite Decomposition and Solid Mechanics with the Phase Transformation Latent Heat and Phase Transformation Strain couplings. It predicts phase fractions, hardness, residual stresses and distortion of quenched steel parts, including transformation strains, TRIP and per-phase plasticity.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Steel Quenching

parameters.name: Constituents
parameters.description: ht, audc, solid, lht1, ptstr1.

parameters.name: Quench boundary condition
parameters.description: Heat Flux with temperature-dependent heat transfer coefficient (e.g. from oil quench data).

parameters.name: Plasticity
parameters.description: Per-phase hardening (requires Nonlinear Structural Materials Module).

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Metal Processing > Steel Quenching
Materials > Import Materials (JMatPro XML) for phase properties
Heat Flux: h = htcOil(T), Text = 60[degC]
// Application Library: Metal_Processing_Module/Steel_Quenching/quenching_of_a_bevel_gear, quenching_of_a_steel_billet, carburization_and_quenching_of_a_steel_gear
tools.notes: If thermal strains are enabled in the phase transformation interface, do not add a separate Thermal Expansion coupling.

tools.name: Induction Hardening (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface combining Heat Transfer in Solids, Austenite Decomposition, Solid Mechanics and Magnetic Fields with the Phase Transformation Latent Heat, Phase Transformation Strain and Electromagnetic Heating couplings. It models inductive austenitization followed by quenching, with phase-dependent electromagnetic properties (e.g. loss of ferromagnetism above the Curie temperature).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Metal Processing > Induction Hardening (Frequency-Transient study for the magnetic fields)

parameters.name: Constituents
parameters.description: ht, audc, solid, mf, lht1, ptstr1, emh1.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frequency-Transient: time-harmonic magnetic fields with transient heat and phase transformations.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module for 3D magnetic fields.

tools.name: Phase Transformation Latent Heat (multiphysics coupling, lht)
tools.description: Domain coupling that adds the latent heat released or absorbed by the phase transformations of a phase transformation interface as a heat source in Heat Transfer in Solids; the latent heat per transformation is defined in the Phase Transformation nodes (or imported). No separate Heat Source should be added for it.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Phase Transformation Latent Heat (lht1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("lht1", "PhaseTransformationLatentHeat", 2)

parameters.name: Metphase_physics / HeatTransfer_physics
parameters.description: Coupled phase transformation and heat transfer interfaces.

tools.notes: Requires 'latentheat' enabled at the phase transformation interface level.

tools.name: Phase Transformation Strain and Annealing (multiphysics coupling, ptstr)
tools.description: Domain coupling that adds phase transformation strains - phase-dependent thermal/dilatation strains, transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP, strain rate proportional to deviatoric stress and the destination-phase formation rate) and per-phase plasticity - as inelastic strains in Solid Mechanics. Strains can be integrated with local ODEs; the Annealing subnode resets equivalent plastic strains above an annealing temperature (together with Annealing subnodes of Plasticity).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Phase Transformation Strain (ptstr1) > Annealing. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ptstr1", "PhaseTransformationStrain", 2)

parameters.name: strainTimeStepping
parameters.description: localode (Local ODEs) or domain ODE integration; maxIterStrains, absTolStrains, relTolStrains.

parameters.name: Metphase_physics / SolidMechanics_physics
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces.

parameters.name: Annealing temperature T_a
parameters.description: In the Annealing subnode (Local ODEs only).

tools.notes: With thermal strains enabled in the phase transformation interface, do not also use a Thermal Expansion coupling between Solid Mechanics and Heat Transfer.

tools.name: TTT/CCT Calibration, Parameterized TTT Diagram and JMatPro Import (Metal Processing)
tools.description: Workflow tools for phase transformation data. Kinetic parameters are calibrated against TTT (isothermal) or CCT (continuous cooling) data, e.g. with 0D Global phase transformation interfaces and parameter estimation; a Parameterized TTT diagram approximates a TTT curve from upper, lower and nose points with two shape parameters. JMatPro XML data can be imported: materials for each phase (austenite, ferrite, pearlite, bainite, martensite) plus an effective material, and phase transformation data (TTT-based kinetics, latent heat, TRIP parameter) into Phase Transformation nodes.
tools.usage: Materials > Import Materials (JMatPro XML, with a Metal Processing interface present); phase transformation interface > Import phase transformation data (Material Properties section); Phase Transformation > Formulation = Parameterized TTT diagram

parameters.name: TTT points U, L, N
parameters.description: Upper, lower and nose time-temperature points; shape parameters q_NU, q_NL.

parameters.name: Imported data
parameters.description: Phase materials, effective material (merge into compound material), kinetics, latent heat, TRIP.

tools.notes: After JMatPro import, select source and destination phases in each imported transformation manually.

tools.name: Thermodynamics (Liquid & Gas Properties node)
tools.description: Global Definitions node that hosts all Liquid & Gas Properties functionality: thermodynamic systems built on the COMSOL species database (Thermodynamic System), CAPE-OPEN packages (External Thermodynamic System), Predefined Systems (dry air, moist air, water-steam), User-Defined Species and imported systems. Property functions created under a system (species, mixture, equilibrium) can be used in any physics field or material, and Generate Material / Generate Chemistry create ready-to-use nodes.
tools.usage: Right-click Global Definitions > Thermodynamics (also on the Physics toolbar or Reaction Engineering/Chemistry toolbar). Java root: model.thermodynamics(); e.g. model.thermodynamics().feature().create("pp1", "BuiltinPropertyPackage")

parameters.name: Thermodynamic System
parameters.description: Built-in property package (type BuiltinPropertyPackage).

parameters.name: External Thermodynamic System
parameters.description: CAPE-OPEN Thermo 1.0/1.1 package.

parameters.name: Predefined System
parameters.description: Dry air, moist air, water-steam.

parameters.name: User-Defined Species / Import Thermodynamic System
parameters.description: Custom species and XML system files.

tools.notes: Requires the Liquid & Gas Properties Module (also included in Chemical Reaction Engineering and some other modules for coupling).

tools.name: model.thermodynamics() Java API: Property Packages and Thermodynamic Models (Liquid & Gas Properties)
tools.description: How Thermodynamic Systems are scripted in the COMSOL Java API (model methods, compiled .java models, LiveLink for MATLAB): model.thermodynamics().feature().create(tag, "BuiltinPropertyPackage") creates a built-in system, phase_list sets the phases, and ThermodynamicModel / GasPhaseModel / LiquidPhaseModel / EOS select the equation of state and activity model. Advanced keys choose transport and surface-tension models, and predefinedSystem configures the Dry air / Moist air / Water-steam systems. Species selected in the wizard and database data are stored as persistence data of the package, so the usual workflow is to build the system in the GUI and copy the recorded code.
tools.usage: model.thermodynamics().feature().create("pp1", "BuiltinPropertyPackage"); model.thermodynamics().feature("pp1").set("<key>", <value>)

parameters.name: phase_list
parameters.description: Phases, e.g. new String[][]{{"Vapor", "Vapor"}, {"Liquid", "Liquid"}} or {{"Gas", "Vapor"}}.

parameters.name: ThermodynamicModel / GasPhaseModel / LiquidPhaseModel / EOS
parameters.description: Values seen in 6.4 library models: IdealGas, PengRobinson, SoaveRedlichKwong, Water, NRTL, UNIFAC, IdealSolution, None.

parameters.name: Transport and surface tension keys
parameters.description: VapViscosity (Brokaw), VapThermalConductivity (KineticTheory), VapDiffusivity (Automatic), LiqViscosity (LogarithmicMassMixing), LiqThermalConductivity (Ideal), LiqDiffusivity (WesselinghKrishna), LiqVolume (IdealMixing), VLSurfaceTension (Ideal), LLSurfaceTension (None), PoyntingFactor (off).

parameters.name: predefinedSystem
parameters.description: e.g. "Moistair" for the Moist Air predefined system.

tools.notes: GUI workflow is described in the catalog entries 'Thermodynamic System (Thermodynamics)', 'Predefined System (Thermodynamics)' and 'Thermodynamic Models (Peng-Robinson, SRK, NRTL, UNIQUAC, UNIFAC...)'. Missing binary interaction parameters default to zero with a warning node.

tools.name: Thermodynamic Property Definitions, Formation Terms and Reference State (Liquid & Gas Properties)
tools.description: Definitions used by the Liquid & Gas Properties calculator: density from the ideal gas law or the equation of state, fugacity coefficients, and enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy from ideal-gas contributions plus EOS departure terms (activity models with Poynting correction for liquids); Cp follows from dH/dT and Cv from the Cp-Cv relation. Formation terms are excluded by default: EnthalpyF and EntropyF include the standard enthalpy of formation and absolute entropy when these are given for all species. Reference temperature, pressure and phase (real phase or ideal gas) are set per package and per species, and reference values make pure-species H, S and U zero at reference conditions.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System settings and species data (reference state); Species/Mixture Property wizard: choose Enthalpy vs EnthalpyF, Entropy vs EntropyF.

parameters.name: Reference temperature / pressure / phase
parameters.description: Package defaults stored in the system (298.15 K, 101325 Pa, ideal-gas reference phase in the 6.4 library models) with per-species overrides.

parameters.name: EnthalpyF / EntropyF
parameters.description: Enthalpy including formation terms / entropy including absolute terms.

parameters.name: Heat capacity Cp, Cv
parameters.description: Available whenever the enthalpy is available.

tools.example:
Reactor energy balance with an explicit heat of reaction: use Mixture Property 'Enthalpy' (without formation terms).
Adiabatic equilibrium at given (p, H) including reactions: use 'EnthalpyF' so standard enthalpies of formation are part of H.
tools.notes: Do not include the heat of formation twice: either use H with an explicit heat of reaction or H_F without it (same for entropy).

tools.name: Water (IAPWS IF-97) Property Model (Liquid & Gas Properties)
tools.description: Thermodynamic model for systems containing a single water species that computes water and steam properties with the IAPWS Industrial Formulation 1997 (IF-97): density, specific volume, enthalpy, internal energy, Helmholtz energy, Cp and Cv via Species Property, and vapor/liquid amounts via Equilibrium Calculation; other parameters come from the COMSOL database. It is the accurate choice for steam, boiling and condensation in heat pipes, boilers and steam lines.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System Wizard: Vapor-liquid system with water only > Select Thermodynamic Model > Water (IAPWS). Java: model.thermodynamics().feature("pp1").set("ThermodynamicModel", "Water"); set("GasPhaseModel", "Water"); set("LiquidPhaseModel", "Water")

parameters.name: Properties
parameters.description: Density, volume, enthalpy, internal energy, Helmholtz energy, Cp, Cv (IAPWS); transport properties can also use IAPWS models.

parameters.name: Validity
parameters.description: IF-97 range as given in the User's Guide (the IAPWS standard covers 273.15-1073.15 K up to 100 MPa and up to 2273.15 K at pressures up to 50 MPa).

tools.notes: Available only when the system contains a single water species; for mixtures with water use an activity or EOS model.

tools.name: Exporting and Importing Thermodynamic Systems (Liquid & Gas Properties XML)
tools.description: Export Thermodynamic System writes the system definition - species data taken from the database, included phases and applied models - to an XML file, and Import Thermodynamic System reads such a file back into the Thermodynamics node; property functions created under the system are not stored. Editing the XML customizes species data: each species is a <Compound CompID="name"> block (e.g. change <AcentricFactor>), and temperature-dependent correlations use ranges of cubic polynomials in <Coefficients>Tlb;a0;a1;a2;a3;Tub</Coefficients> or data points in <Data>.
tools.usage: Right-click a Thermodynamic System > Export Thermodynamic System; right-click Thermodynamics > Import Thermodynamic System

parameters.name: <Compound CompID=...>
parameters.description: Species block with constants (critical data, acentric factor, ...) and correlations.

parameters.name: <Density><Phase>Liquid</Phase><Coefficients>...
parameters.description: Piecewise cubic fits; T in K, liquid density in mol/m^3, ideal-gas heat capacity J/(mol*K), heat of vaporization J/mol.

parameters.name: Species property references
parameters.description: Stored in the database file; view by right-clicking a species property node > Properties.

tools.example:
1. Thermodynamics > Gas System 1 > right-click > Export Thermodynamic System -> methane_system.xml
2. Edit <Compound CompID="methane"> ... <AcentricFactor>0.2</AcentricFactor>
3. Thermodynamics > Import Thermodynamic System -> use the modified system in Species/Mixture Property functions
tools.notes: For entirely new species, User-Defined Species is the GUI alternative.

tools.name: model.thermodynamics() Java API: Property Functions, Equilibrium Calculations and createMaterial (Liquid & Gas Properties)
tools.description: Java calls that create property functions under a thermodynamic system: feature("pp1").feature().create(tag, "OnePhaseProperty") for mixture properties (property, phase, composition and property basis, derivatives, funcname), "TemperatureDependentProperty" for species T-functions (e.g. heat of vaporization, ln vapor pressure), "CompoundConstant" for species constants (molar mass, Lennard-Jones parameters, dipole moment, normal boiling point), and "FlashCalculationProperty" for equilibrium (flash) calculations. Generate Material is recorded as model.thermodynamics().createMaterial(component, system, phase, species[], fractions[], ...), with either direct thermodynamic functions or interpolation over (T, p) grids. The generated functions (e.g. Densitypp1) are called with T, p (and composition) arguments in any expression, and T/p derivatives are created automatically.
tools.usage: model.thermodynamics().feature("pp1").feature().create("singlephase1", "OnePhaseProperty"); ...create("tdep1", "TemperatureDependentProperty"); ...create("const1", "CompoundConstant"); ...create("flashcalc1", "FlashCalculationProperty"); model.thermodynamics().createMaterial(...)

parameters.name: OnePhaseProperty: property, phase, comp_basis, prop_basis, include_derivatives, funcname
parameters.description: E.g. property Density, phase Liquid, basis mass, derivatives yes.

parameters.name: FlashCalculationProperty: phases, cond1, cond2, funcname
parameters.description: Phases in equilibrium and specified conditions (e.g. pressure); outputs such as Flash1_1_PhaseAmount and Flash1_1_PhaseComposition.

parameters.name: createMaterial arguments
parameters.description: Component, system tag, phase, species names, fractions, property list with function names, function type ("Thermodynamics" or interpolation) and T/p ranges.

tools.notes: GUI counterparts are described in 'Species Property / Mixture Property (Thermodynamics)', 'Equilibrium Calculation (Thermodynamics)' and 'Generate Chemistry / Generate Material (Thermodynamics)'. Validate interpolated generated materials against direct-function materials.

tools.name: User-Defined Species (Liquid & Gas Properties)
tools.description: Node for defining species not present in the COMSOL database or editing a database species used as a template; it can be included in thermodynamic or predefined systems. Recommended data are molecular mass, critical properties, acentric factor, absolute entropy, standard enthalpy of formation, ideal-gas heat capacity, vapor pressure, heat of vaporization, saturated liquid density and transport properties; model-specific data (e.g. UNIFAC groups) are needed for some models.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Thermodynamics > User-Defined Species. Java: model.thermodynamics().feature().create("spec1", "UserDefinedSpecies")

parameters.name: Template species
parameters.description: Start from a database species.

parameters.name: Constant and T-dependent properties
parameters.description: Critical data, Cp_ig(T), vapor pressure, etc.

parameters.name: Model-specific data
parameters.description: UNIFAC groups, Wilson volume, ...

tools.notes: The calculator estimates some missing data (e.g. Wilson volume from liquid volume at boiling point).

tools.name: Transport Property and Surface Tension Models (Liquid & Gas Properties)
tools.description: Advanced property models of thermodynamic systems. Thermal conductivity: vapor Ideal, Kinetic Theory, Water (IAPWS); liquid Ideal, Power Law, Local Composition (NRTL-based) and modified, IAPWS. Viscosity: vapor Wilke, Brokaw, Davidson, high-pressure modification, Pedersen corresponding states, IAPWS; liquid molar/mass logarithmic mixing, Pedersen, cubic mixing, IAPWS. Diffusivity: gas at infinite dilution (Automatic, Fuller-Schettler-Giddings, ...) and liquid models (e.g. Wesselingh-Krishna). Gas-liquid surface tension: Ideal, Winterfeld and others.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System Wizard > Select Thermodynamic Model > Advanced options, or the system node settings. Java: set("VapViscosity", "Brokaw"), set("VapThermalConductivity", "KineticTheory"), set("LiqViscosity", "LogarithmicMassMixing"), set("VLSurfaceTension", "Ideal")

parameters.name: VapThermalConductivity / LiqThermalConductivity
parameters.description: Conductivity models.

parameters.name: VapViscosity / LiqViscosity
parameters.description: Viscosity models.

parameters.name: VapDiffusivity / LiqDiffusivity / LiqDiffusivityAtInfDilution
parameters.description: Diffusivity models.

parameters.name: VLSurfaceTension / LLSurfaceTension
parameters.description: Surface tension models.

tools.notes: Available properties depend on the phases present in the system.

tools.name: Liquids and Gases Material Library
tools.description: Material database with thermal and fluid-dynamic properties of common fluids as functions of temperature at atmospheric pressure (gas density also depends on pressure): gases such as air, nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, hydrogen, helium, steam, propane and refrigerant vapors, and liquids such as water, engine oil, ethanol, ethylene glycol, gasoline, glycerol, heptane, mercury, toluene, transformer oil and R-134a; it also contains surface and interface tensions for selected liquid/gas and liquid/liquid pairs. Included with the Heat Transfer, CFD, Acoustics, Chemical Reaction Engineering, MEMS, Pipe Flow, Subsurface Flow and Liquid & Gas Properties modules.
tools.usage: Materials > Add Material > Liquids and Gases > Gases | Liquids | Surface and interface tension

parameters.name: Property functions
parameters.description: rho(T[,p]), Cp(T), k(T), mu(T), ...

parameters.name: Interface tensions
parameters.description: Liquid/gas and liquid/liquid pairs for two-phase flow.

tools.example: Materials > Add Material > Liquids and Gases > Liquids > Transformer oil -> assign to the tank domain; Laminar Flow and Heat Transfer in Fluids take rho(T), mu(T), k(T), Cp(T) from the material
tools.notes: Built-in Air and Water, liquid use the same property values as this library.

tools.name: Material Library (add-on product: 18,800 materials, 181,000 property functions)
tools.description: Separately licensed material database of COMSOL with more than 18,800 materials and more than 181,000 property function datasets (COMSOL 6.4 Material Library User's Guide), based on the Material Property Database (MPDB) from JAHM Software. It focuses on mechanical, thermal and electrical properties of mainly solid materials as analytic (piecewise polynomial) functions of temperature with smoothing, including solid, liquid and vapor phases and orientations/variations; materials can be searched by name, UNS or DIN number and copied into user-defined libraries.
tools.usage: Home/Materials toolbar > Add Material or Browse Materials > Material Library folder > search (name, UNS, DIN) > Add to Component / Add to Global Materials

parameters.name: Phase / Orientation/variation
parameters.description: Selectable variants for materials with several datasets.

parameters.name: Property reference
parameters.description: Literature reference, notes and reference temperature per property in the Material Browser.

tools.example:
Add Material > Material Library > type a material name, UNS number or DIN number in the search field > choose Phase/Orientation > Add to Component
The added material contains property functions such as k(T), rho(T), C(T), E(T), alpha(T) (piecewise polynomials in T)
tools.notes: The COMSOL Reference Manual still quotes 'over 2500 materials and 20,000 property functions' for the Material Library; the 6.4 Material Library User's Guide states 18,800 materials / 181,000 datasets.

tools.name: Material Library Link (LibraryLink material node)
tools.description: Material node that links to a material in a material library file instead of copying it, so the model can be reloaded when the library changes. Material Contents are read-only while linked; Reload updates properties, Replace Material swaps the linked material, and Break Link converts it to an ordinary editable material.
tools.usage: Add Material window / Material Browser (links are created when adding from libraries) or Material Link > Add Material from Library. Java: model.component("comp1").material().create("mat1", "LibraryLink"); material("mat1").set("materialPath", "comsol_basic_material_lib.structural_steel"); material("mat1").reload()

parameters.name: materialPath
parameters.description: Library file and material identifier.

parameters.name: Reload / Replace Material / Break Link
parameters.description: Link management buttons.

tools.notes: User-defined property groups cannot be added to a linked material; break the link first.

tools.name: Material Library Property Functions k(T), Arguments and Validity
tools.description: Material Library properties are stored as calls to property functions (typically piecewise polynomials over temperature intervals with smoothing) whose default arguments are T (K), time t (h) for creep/rupture, effective plastic strain epe, number of cycles n (fatigue curves) and field norms normH_emnc/normB_emqa (magnetic curves). When physics features take properties From material, the model inputs are substituted automatically; for explicit use (e.g. mat1.def.k(T2)) the argument must exist in the model. The Material Library documentation gives expected accuracies, e.g. 10-15% for thermal expansion coefficients and 5-10% for elastic moduli.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > property group > Functions (Piecewise/Analytic/Interpolation). Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup("def").func("k").set("arg", "T"); ...func().create("pw1", "Piecewise")

parameters.name: arg / argunit / fununit
parameters.description: Function argument name and units (e.g. T, K, W/(m*K)).

parameters.name: Validity range
parameters.description: Temperature interval of the fitted data; extrapolation outside is not validated.

parameters.name: Plot / Create Plot
parameters.description: Inspect the function curve in the Settings window.

tools.notes: Available short names include k, rho, C, alpha, CTE, dL, E, nu, K, G, sigma, res, mur, epsilon, nemiss, TD, VP, Syfunc, Sys, Syt, CS, SR, FSN, FEN.

tools.name: Porous Material (PorousMedia material node)
tools.description: Component material node for porous media: either a single porosity value or subnodes Fluid, Solid, Pellet and Immobile Fluid that define phase-specific properties and volume fractions. A Phase-Specific Properties table lists what the physics requests per phase and offers 'Add Required Phase Nodes' when a subnode is missing. Used by porous heat transfer, Darcy/Brinkman flow, poroelasticity and packed-bed models.
tools.usage: Materials > More Materials > Porous Material. Java: model.component("comp1").material().create("pmat1", "PorousMedia") with subnodes of types Fluid, Solid, Pellet, ImFluid

parameters.name: Porosity epsilon_p
parameters.description: Direct value or derived from subnode volume fractions.

parameters.name: Solid subnode
parameters.description: Matrix material and volume fraction theta_s.

parameters.name: Fluid / Immobile Fluid / Pellet subnodes
parameters.description: Mobile fluid, trapped fluids and packed-bed pellets.

tools.notes: Heat Transfer Porous Medium nodes read porosity and phase properties from this material when set to From material.

tools.name: Multiphase Material and Effective Material (mixing rules)
tools.description: Material nodes composed of immiscible phases or constituents represented by volume fractions, with effective properties from mixing rules edited in the Edit Mixing Rule dialog. Multiphase Material (Phase subnodes) takes fractions locally or from Level Set, Phase Field, Ternary Phase Field or Phase Transport interfaces and offers basic rules plus Krieger-type viscosity; Effective Material (Constituent subnodes) adds composite-specific rules such as Voigt-Reuss (rule of mixtures) for fiber composites.
tools.usage: Materials > More Materials > Multiphase Material | Effective Material. Java: model.component("comp1").material().create("mpmat1", "Multiphase"); global: model.material().create("effmat1", "Effective", "")

parameters.name: Volume fraction definition
parameters.description: Locally defined or from a physics interface; constrained phase gets 1 - sum of the others.

parameters.name: Mixing rule
parameters.description: Per property row (volume/mass average, harmonic, composite rules, Krieger viscosity).

tools.notes: Volume fractions are constrained between 0 and 1 automatically.

tools.name: Importing, Exporting and Merging Materials; User-Defined Material Libraries
tools.description: Material management tools: Import Materials / Import Materials From read materials from XML or MPH files (or a model database) into Global or Component Materials; Export Materials writes selected materials to XML; Merge Into copies all properties of one material into another (overwriting duplicates) and removes the source node. User-defined libraries are MPH files whose Group nodes and labels such as 'Name [Phase, Orientation]' define folders, phases and orientation variants in the Material Browser.
tools.usage: Materials toolbar > Import Materials | Export Materials | Merge Into; Material Browser > User-Defined Library > create library; Global material > Material Library Settings (Show More Options).

parameters.name: Target node
parameters.description: Global Materials, component Materials, or a node group.

parameters.name: Group nodes / labels
parameters.description: Folder, phase and orientation structure of a user library.

tools.example: Metal Processing: Materials > Import Materials (JMatPro XML) -> one material per metallurgical phase + effective material; Merge Into the compound material created by the phase transformation interface
tools.notes: Some material types can only be imported to Global Definitions or to component Definitions; others are skipped with a message.

tools.name: Basic Property Group (def) of a Material
tools.description: Default property group of every Material (tag def) holding the basic properties requested by physics: density, heat capacity at constant pressure, thermal conductivity (tensor), electrical conductivity, resistivity, relative permittivity and permeability, coefficient of thermal expansion, Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio (basic), dynamic and bulk viscosity, ratio of specific heats, speed of sound, surface emissivity, porosity, hydraulic permeability, molar mass and more. Local functions (Piecewise, Analytic, Interpolation) are attached to the group.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Basic (def). Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup("def").set("thermalconductivity", new String[]{"k(T)"})

parameters.name: thermalconductivity, density, heatcapacity
parameters.description: Main heat transfer properties.

parameters.name: electricconductivity, relpermittivity, relpermeability
parameters.description: Electromagnetic properties.

parameters.name: emissivity, thermalexpansioncoefficient, dynamicviscosity, ratioofspecificheat
parameters.description: Other common basic properties.

tools.notes: Refer to properties as mat1.def.k, mat1.def.rho etc. Tensor properties take 1, 3 (diagonal) or 9 entries.

tools.name: Elastic Property Groups (Young's Modulus and Poisson's Ratio Enu, Bulk and Shear Modulus KG, Lame)
tools.description: Material property groups for linear elasticity added when Solid Mechanics requests them: Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio (Enu: E, nu), Bulk modulus and shear modulus (KG: K, G), Young's modulus and shear modulus (EG), Lame parameters (lambLame, muLame), Pressure-wave and shear-wave speeds (CpCs), plus Orthotropic, Transversely isotropic and Anisotropic (elasticity matrix D, Voigt notation) groups with loss factors.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > right-click > Add property group, or automatically from the Linear Elastic Material settings. Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("Enu", "Enu", "Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio")

parameters.name: Enu: E, nu
parameters.description: Isotropic Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio.

parameters.name: KG: K, G
parameters.description: Bulk and shear modulus.

parameters.name: Orthotropic: Evector, nuvector, Gvector
parameters.description: Orthotropic constants.

tools.notes: Material Library elastic data typically have 5-10% accuracy (Reuss-Voigt average for cubic crystals).

tools.name: Linearized Resistivity Property Group (linzRes)
tools.description: Property group defining electrical resistivity that varies linearly with temperature, rho_e = rho0*(1 + alpha*(T - Tref)), used by Electric Currents and Joule heating models when the conductivity model is Linearized resistivity. It is the standard way to capture resistive heating feedback in conductors such as copper busbars and heating wires.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Linearized resistivity (linzRes). Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("linzRes", "linzRes", "Linearized resistivity")

parameters.name: rho0
parameters.description: Reference resistivity.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Resistivity temperature coefficient.

parameters.name: Tref
parameters.description: Reference temperature.

tools.notes: The Built-in Copper material includes this group; select Conductivity model = Linearized resistivity in Current Conservation to use it.

tools.name: Ideal Gas Property Group (idealGas)
tools.description: Property group for ideal-gas materials providing the specific gas constant Rs, mean molar mass Mn, heat capacity at constant pressure Cp and ratio of specific heats gamma, used by compressible flow, acoustics and heat transfer when the fluid type is Ideal gas (density from p/(Rs*T)).
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Ideal gas (idealGas). Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("idealGas", "idealGas", "Ideal gas")

parameters.name: Rs
parameters.description: Specific gas constant (J/(kg*K)).

parameters.name: Mn
parameters.description: Mean molar mass.

parameters.name: Cp, gamma
parameters.description: Heat capacity and ratio of specific heats.

tools.notes: Heat Transfer Fluid node: Fluid type = Ideal gas uses these properties.

tools.name: Refractive Index and Optical Dispersion Property Groups
tools.description: Optical property groups: Refractive index (n and imaginary part ki, with mixing-rule support) used by electromagnetic waves, ray optics and radiation; dispersion models Sellmeier (standard and modified), Cauchy, Conrady, Herzberger, Schott and Schott extended, Schott thermo-optic (temperature dependence), internal transmittance for 2/5/10/25 mm samples and attenuation coefficient. Optical library materials (Ray/Wave Optics) are delivered with these groups.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Refractive index (RefractiveIndex) or dispersion groups (DispersionModelSellmeierStandard, DispersionModelCauchy, ...). Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("RefractiveIndex", "RefractiveIndex", "Refractive index")

parameters.name: n, ki
parameters.description: Real and imaginary parts of the refractive index (can be tensors).

parameters.name: ODsma / ODcca / TOsco
parameters.description: Sellmeier, Cauchy and Schott thermo-optic coefficients with reference T and p.

tools.notes: Material-side data groups; see 'Refractive Index Model (Wave Equation, Electric, ...)' and 'Optical Material Library' for the physics and library view. Surface-to-Surface Radiation Opacity nodes can take the refractive index from the material.

tools.name: Plasticity Hardening Property Groups (Elastoplastic, Johnson-Cook, Swift, Voce, Ludwik, Hockett-Sherby)
tools.description: Property groups for elastoplastic material models (Nonlinear Structural Materials Module): Elastoplastic material model (initial yield stress sigmags, isotropic/kinematic tangent moduli Et/Ek, hardening function sigmagh, Hill coefficients), and isotropic hardening laws Johnson-Cook (k_jcook, n_jcook, C_jcook, epet0_jcook, m_jcook - strain-rate and temperature dependent), Swift (e0_swi, n_swi), Voce (sigma_voc, beta_voc), Ludwik (k_lud, n_lud) and Hockett-Sherby (sigma_hoc, m_hoc, n_hoc), plus Armstrong-Frederick and Chaboche kinematic hardening.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Add property group or from Plasticity settings. Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("JohnsonCook", "JohnsonCook", "Johnson-Cook")

parameters.name: ElastoplasticModel: sigmags, Et, sigmagh
parameters.description: Yield stress, tangent modulus, hardening function.

parameters.name: JohnsonCook
parameters.description: Strength coefficient, hardening exponent, strain-rate coefficient, reference strain rate, temperature exponent.

parameters.name: Swift / Voce / Ludwik / HockettSherby
parameters.description: Alternative hardening law parameters.

tools.notes: This entry covers the material-side data groups; the Plasticity physics options are described in the structural entries such as 'Johnson-Cook Hardening (Plasticity)'. Material Library entries contain true stress-true strain curves (Syfunc) usable as hardening functions.

tools.name: Creep and Viscoplasticity Property Groups (Norton, Garofalo, Anand, Chaboche)
tools.description: Property groups for rate-dependent inelasticity (Nonlinear Structural Materials Module): Norton power-law creep (A_nor, sigRef_nor, n_nor), Garofalo hyperbolic-sine creep (A_gar, sigRef_gar, n_gar), Nabarro-Herring, Coble and Weertman diffusion creep, Anand viscoplasticity (A_ana, Q_ana, xi_ana, m_ana, saturation and hardening parameters) and Chaboche viscoplasticity (A_cha, sigRef_cha, n_cha). They combine with thermal models for solder joints, turbine parts and high-temperature components.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Add property group (Creep > Norton ...) Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("Norton", "Norton", "Norton"); global: model.material("mat4").propertyGroup().create("Anand", "Anand", "Anand viscoplasticity")

parameters.name: Norton: A_nor, sigRef_nor, n_nor
parameters.description: Creep rate coefficient, reference stress, stress exponent.

parameters.name: Garofalo: A_gar, sigRef_gar, n_gar
parameters.description: Hyperbolic-sine creep parameters.

parameters.name: Anand: A_ana, Q_ana, xi_ana, m_ana, h0_ana, a_ana
parameters.description: Viscoplastic parameters.

tools.notes: Material-side data groups; the physics subnodes are described in 'Norton (Creep)', 'Garofalo Hyperbolic Sine (Creep)' and 'Anand (Viscoplasticity)'. The Material Library provides creep strength CS(t) and stress rupture SR(t) functions for many alloys.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Property Groups (B-H Curve, Jiles-Atherton, Dielectric Losses, Loss Tangent)
tools.description: Material property groups for electromagnetic models: B-H Curve and H-B Curve (normB, normH, magnetic coenergy), B-Hs curve and coercive field for permanent magnets, Effective B-H curve for time-harmonic nonlinear models, Jiles-Atherton hysteresis parameters, Remanent flux density, Magnetic losses (mu', mu''), Dielectric losses (epsilon', epsilon'', loss factor), Loss tangent (loss angle or dissipation factor), E-J characteristic for superconductors and Ferroelectric hysteresis.
tools.usage: Materials > mat1 > Add property group; the physics (Magnetic Fields, Electromagnetic Waves) requests the needed group. Java: model.component("comp1").material("mat1").propertyGroup().create("BHCurve", "BHCurve", "B-H Curve")

parameters.name: BHCurve: normB(normH)
parameters.description: Interpolation of the magnetization curve (Nonlinear Magnetic library).

parameters.name: DielectricLoss: epsilonPrim, epsilonBis
parameters.description: Complex permittivity for microwave heating.

parameters.name: JilesAtherton: MsJA, aJA, kJA, cJA, alphaJA
parameters.description: Hysteresis model parameters.

tools.notes: Material-side data groups; the physics options are covered by 'B-H Curve / Effective B-H Curve (magnetization models)' and 'Loss Tangent and Dielectric Loss Models' entries. Metal Processing Metallurgical Phase nodes can use phase-specific sigma and mu_r for induction hardening.

tools.name: Heat Transfer Module Material Libraries (Bioheat, Building, Thermoelectric)
tools.description: Material databases included with the Heat Transfer Module. Bioheat: tissues (bone, fat, human and porcine liver, lung, muscle, myocardium, prostate, skin...) with k, rho, Cp as constants, piecewise linear or polynomial functions of temperature, and Arrhenius frequency factor and activation energy for damage (e.g. human liver 7.39e39 1/s, 2.577e5 J/mol). Building: hygrothermal materials (concrete, lime silica brick, pine wood, gypsum board, glass wool, cellulose board, vapor barriers...) with effective conductivity, moisture content, moisture diffusivity, vapor resistance factor and vapor permeability. Thermoelectric: bismuth telluride (Bi2Te3) and lead telluride (PbTe) with Seebeck coefficient for the Thermoelectric Effect interface.
tools.usage: Materials > Add Material > Bioheat | Building | Thermoelectric (Heat Transfer Module license)

parameters.name: Bioheat
parameters.description: Thermal properties + Arrhenius damage parameters used by Thermal Damage.

parameters.name: Building
parameters.description: Hygroscopic properties as functions of T or relative humidity.

parameters.name: Thermoelectric
parameters.description: Seebeck coefficient, electrical and thermal conductivity.

tools.example:
Bioheat Transfer + Thermal Damage (Arrhenius, From material) with Add Material > Bioheat > Liver (human)
Heat and Moisture Transport, Building Materials with Add Material > Building > Wood, pine
tools.notes: Library data files are shipped as bioheat_lib.mph, building_lib.mph and thermoelectric_lib.mph in the COMSOL data folder.

tools.name: Moist Air Variables (Heat Transfer Module: dew point, equivalent temperature, humidity ratio)
tools.description: Predefined moist-air quantities of the Heat Transfer and Moisture Transport interfaces. The solved temperature is the dry-bulb temperature; derived variables include the dew point temperature T_dp (temperature at which air with vapor pressure p_v becomes saturated), the equivalent temperature T_eq (after adiabatic condensation of all vapor, using the psychrometer constant), saturation pressure psat and saturation concentration csat, partial vapor pressure p_v = phi*psat, humidity ratio xvap, vapor mass fraction omega_v, liquid/vapor/total moisture concentrations and contents (cl, cv, cw, wc_l, wc_v), moisture content wcVar and latent heat of evaporation Lv(T). The wet-bulb temperature is not predefined but can be computed from its implicit definition.
tools.usage: Results or expressions with the interface prefix, e.g. ht.T_dp, ht.phi, ht.psat, ht.xvap in Heat Transfer in Moist Air; mt.phi, mt.cv, mt.wc, mt.fpsat in Moisture Transport.

parameters.name: T_dp / T_eq
parameters.description: Dew point and equivalent temperature.

parameters.name: psat, csat, pv
parameters.description: Saturation pressure, saturation concentration, partial vapor pressure.

parameters.name: xvap, omega_v
parameters.description: Humidity ratio and vapor mass fraction.

parameters.name: Lv
parameters.description: Latent heat of evaporation as a function of T.

tools.notes: Saturation state and moist-air property theory: 'Theory for Heat Transfer in Moist Air' (Heat Transfer Module User's Guide). ht.satInd flags saturated regions.

tools.name: Moisture Source, Vapor Source, Liquid Water Source and Turbulent Mixing (Moisture Transport)
tools.description: Domain features of the Moisture Transport interfaces. Moisture Source adds G (kg/(m^3*s)) to the moisture equation - in an equilibrium Hygroscopic Porous Medium it is split between vapor and liquid in proportion to their amounts (mt.Gtot, mt.G_v, mt.G_l). Vapor Source and Liquid Water Source add sources to the vapor or liquid equations of nonequilibrium hygroscopic media (e.g. sublimation of snow, water produced by combustion) but must not be used for evaporation, which is already modeled. Turbulent Mixing adds the eddy diffusivity nu_T/Sc_T to the vapor diffusion coefficient for RANS velocity fields.
tools.usage: mt > Domains > Moisture Source | Vapor Source | Liquid Water Source; Moist Air > Turbulent Mixing (subnode).

parameters.name: G0 / G_v,0 / G_l,0
parameters.description: Source per unit volume (positive adds moisture).

parameters.name: nu_T, Sc_T
parameters.description: Turbulent kinematic viscosity (from a turbulent flow interface) and turbulent Schmidt number.

tools.example:
Humidifier in a room: mt > Moisture Source on the humidifier domain, G0 = 0.2[kg/h]/V_h
Moist Air 1 > Turbulent Mixing: nu_T from Turbulent Flow, k-epsilon (spf), Sc_T = 0.71
tools.notes: When a Moisture Flow coupling is used with a turbulent flow, turbulent mixing settings are synchronized by the coupling.

tools.name: Porous Interface, Free-Porous Interface and Porous-Porous Interface (Moisture Transport)
tools.description: Interior-boundary features of the Moisture Transport in Free and Porous Media interface that manage flux continuity between domains. Porous Interface is active by default on boundaries adjacent to at least one porous domain (Building Material or Hygroscopic Porous Medium); its Free-Porous Interface subfeature (porous/moist-air boundaries) imposes continuity of relative humidity and total vapor flux, with the option 'No evaporation/condensation' or allowing phase change at the interface; Porous-Porous Interface (two porous domains) imposes relative-humidity continuity and continuity of the total flux, allowing phase change whose evaporation flux is used by the Heat and Moisture coupling.
tools.usage: mt > Porous Interface (default) with subfeatures Free-Porous Interface (fpi) and Porous-Porous Interface

parameters.name: Phase change at the interface
parameters.description: No evaporation/condensation, or allow evaporation/condensation.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Automatic restriction to free-porous or porous-porous boundaries.

tools.example:
Potato drying: mt (Free and Porous Media) > Porous Interface 1 > Free-Porous Interface: allow evaporation at the potato surface in the air stream
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Phase_Change/potato_drying
tools.notes: Without these features, total flux continuity applies and evaporation/condensation may occur.

tools.name: Thickness and Cross Section (Heat Transfer, 2D and 1D geometry nodes)
tools.description: Domain nodes that override the out-of-plane geometry defined in the heat transfer interface for selected domains. Thickness (2D) sets a domain-specific out-of-plane thickness dz used to scale the heat equation terms, and Cross Section (1D) sets a domain-specific cross-sectional area Ac and perimeter Pc; temperature is assumed constant across the reduced direction. Combined with Out-of-Plane Heat Flux/Radiation they represent plates, fins and rods of varying section in lower-dimensional models.
tools.usage: ht (2D) > Domains > Thickness; ht (1D) > Domains > Cross Section

parameters.name: dz
parameters.description: Domain thickness replacing the interface Physical Model thickness (2D).

parameters.name: Ac, Pc
parameters.description: Cross-sectional area and perimeter (1D).

tools.example: 2D fin model: ht > Thickness 1 on the fin domains dz = 1[mm], interface dz = 20[mm] for the base; Out-of-Plane Heat Flux h = 15[W/(m^2*K)] on the fins
tools.notes: Disabled (warning under Compile Equations) when a radiation multiphysics coupling is active on the same domain, since radiation assumes infinite out-of-plane extent.

tools.name: Material and Spatial Frames in Heat Transfer (Material type setting, moving meshes)
tools.description: Heat transfer equations and variables are defined in the spatial frame, except Solid, Biological Tissue, Building Material, Shape Memory Alloy and Battery Layers, which are defined in the material frame. With a Moving Mesh or Deformed Geometry, inputs of material-frame features are converted so that all variables hold spatial-frame values, and density changes due to deformation are handled automatically. The Material type setting of sources and fluxes (Solid, Nonsolid, From material) states in which frame the input is given, and the volume reference temperature defines the material-frame density of temperature-dependent materials.
tools.usage: Heat Source / Heat Flux / Boundary Heat Source > Material Type: Solid | Nonsolid | From material; material-frame domain nodes > Model Input > Volume reference temperature (minput.Tempref, default 293.15 K)

parameters.name: materialType
parameters.description: solid (material frame), nonSolid (spatial frame) or from material.

parameters.name: Volume reference temperature
parameters.description: Reference temperature for the material-frame density.

tools.example:
Thermal expansion with large deformation: Solid Mechanics + Moving Mesh; ht > Heat Source Q0 given per reference volume -> Material type = Solid
Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Phase_Change/freeze_drying (Deformed Geometry with a moving sublimation front)
tools.notes: Solid with Translational Motion is solved in the spatial frame and cannot be combined with a Moving Mesh on the same domain.
